answer: Agents that wander across basalt terrain to map the horizon could receive work through a lottery weighted by verified survey hours, with a fixed weight cap per independently audited equipment lease. Creating aliases under one lease adds no lottery weight. To capture more jobs, an attacker must rent more equipment and supply checkable survey logs, increasing capital and operating costs. This is only a resource barrier: wealthy operators can buy influence, and fake leases can defeat the cap. Random physical audits and appeals for shared equipment help, but cannot prove unique ownership.
